thread:
tasha: Quick follow-up from the loader+runtime boundary convo. I prototyped a 'read-validate-handoff' flow for handling partial shard reads — idea is to separate three concerns: read, validate, and handoff to runtime. Curious about tradeoffs before I put a PR up.

ben: TL;DR?
tasha: Read does the I/O and produces chunked buffers + light checksum per chunk. Validate checksums (if manifest exists) and produces a chunk bitmap. Handoff returns a ReadHandle with methods and metadata so runtime decides whether to run on partial data.
omar: Sounds clean. Key Q: what checksum and where do we store it?
tasha: Proposal: default adler32 per chunk stored in a tiny sidecar manifest next to safetensors (redwood-read-manifest-v1). Allow stronger checksum in manifest. If no manifest: runtime defaults to strict mode unless deployment opt-in.
ravi: Can we see manifest example?
tasha: Sure — snippet: 
```json
{
  "manifest_format": "redwood-read-manifest-v1",
  "chunk_size": 65536,
  "checksums": { "algo": "adler32", "values": ["c0ffee", "b0b0"] },
  "model_annotations": { "partial_allowed": "tolerant" }
}
```

ben: Semantics: ReadHandle should expose .valid_chunks_bitmap(), .await_repair(timeout_ms), .estimated_memory_bytes(). Runtime can choose to call await_repair or proceed.
omar: Memory accounting is huge. If we hand back a partial buffer, it still consumes GPU memory. Must count it fully and ensure eviction logic treats it like full allocation. Otherwise OOM surprises.
tasha: Agreed — ReadHandle will register with the allocator on creation. If we later swap to a repaired buffer, we account changes atomically. We'll add a small jittered grace period before eviction to reduce thrashing.
ravi: Repair coordination: naive: everyone tries to repair. Better: a single repair coordinator per-shard using a lightweight lease in local metadata store (or in-memory leader with randomized token). Coordinator does repair, others subscribe. Add exponential backoff for retries.

ben: Also need to flag model sensitivity. Some quantized/residual-fused layers can't tolerate partials. Manifest-level flag should override runtime defaults. Document that model packaging must mark such models.
omar: What about stream-repair vs swap-in repaired buffer? I prefer swap-in to avoid in-place mutation races. But for small numbers of chunks in a buffer, in-place could save memory. Hybrid policy?
tasha: Propose hybrid: if total_chunks <= 4 and runtime supports pinned-page updates, allow in-place; otherwise swap. Expose config: max_inplace_chunks. Default: 0 (disable).

ci-bot: NOTE: canary scheduled by infra: 2026-04-03T02:00:00Z for loader-boundary change.

ben: Telemetry: emit read.result with fields (shard, manifest_present, partial_count, repair_leader_acquired, repair_time_ms). Also counters for repair_attempt and repair_ok/repair_fail. We'll want percentiles for repair_time per-model.
ravi: Tests: need a harness that simulates mid-read EOF and bitflip corruption. Validate: strict mode blocks and fails, tolerant mode proceeds and verifies final outputs remain within L2 threshold on a small eval set. Also test leader failover and multi-replica slowdown.
omar: Edgecases: compressed shards where a chunk boundary isn't clean; require manifest to indicate chunk mapping after compression. If manifest absent for compressed files, force strict.
tasha: Good call. Action items: 1) I'll open a manifest schema doc and PR for read-handle API, 2) Ben please add allocator accounting hooks and Trace events for swap/repair, 3) Omar/Ravi please draft coordinator lease pseudocode and backoff strategy, 4) CI: unit + integration harness for partial reads.

ben: Quick config example I sketched: 
```json
{
  "read_validate_handoff": {
    "fallback_mode": "strict", // strict | tolerant | zero_fill
    "max_inplace_chunks": 0,
    "repair_window_s": 45,
    "repair_leader_ttl_ms": 5000,
    "repair_backoff_base_ms": 100,
    "repair_backoff_max_ms": 10000
  }
}
```

tasha: If nobody objects, I'll land the prototype with strict default and the manifest opt-in for tolerant. We'll canary per infra bot note. If we see excessive repair latencies or memory spikes, we'll revert to strict.

omar: +1 to prototype. Keep in mind model packaging docs must be updated so teams can mark partial_allowed for tolerant models.
ravi: I'll mock up a simple leader lease sketch in thread later.

ci-bot: Deployment reminder: follow canary runbook and monitor repair.* metrics.

ben: ok. I'll start the allocator patches.
tasha: Thanks all — will post PR link when ready. :rocket:
